prerequisites: Ability to abstract: translate from colloquial language to mathematical language (and vice versa).
Handle and understand basic mathematical symbology (e.g. summation).
Handle and understand the real function with real variable.
Apply the concept of derivative and integral in one variable to elementary functions.
Use basic knowledge of the applications of the concept of a function limit.
Transform units from one scale to another.
Contents from Mathematics II or Mathematics applied to Social Sciences in 2nd year of Bachillerato.
Contents corresponding to Bachillerato Mathematics subjects.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, enabling them to learn new methods and technologies, and providing them with great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunication Technologies and Services Engineer.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task planning and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunication.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases and computer programs with application in engineering.
Collect statistical data, present it clearly and concisely, and analyze the results.
Make predictions for different working conditions and estimate their reliability.
Use statistical models in solving real problems.
Make decisions in an uncertain environment.
Handle the different measurement scales and their possibilities in statistical analysis.
Discriminate between the objectives of a statistical analysis: descriptive and inferential.
Distinguish between a statistical population and a sample from it.
Understand the information provided by a statistical table that orders sample data.
Summarize sample information using measures of central tendency, dispersion, and position.
Compare information obtained from different samples.
Recognize the degree of dependence between different characteristics of a sample.
Model the dependence between different characteristics of the sample using a function (linear or non-linear). Use the model for prediction and assess its reliability.
Know the probabilistic basis of Statistical Inference.
Apply basic probability calculation concepts to problem solving.
Assign statistical models to different real-life behaviors. Identify different probability distributions.
Use descriptive techniques for classification and obtaining information through characteristic parameters of the analyzed sample or population.
Estimate unknown parameters of a population from a sample.
Handle principles and applications of statistical hypothesis tests.
Formulate real problems in statistical terms (parameter estimation, hypothesis testing,...) and apply Statistical Inference to their resolution.
Be proficient in the use of tables, calculators and statistical packages.
Know the theoretical foundations and concepts related to these problems.
Be able to reason and justify their solutions to statistics problems based on evidence.
Be able to use Statistics as a necessary tool in their future professional practice.

syllabus_topics: Measures of central tendency, position and dispersion.
Fundamental theorems in probability. Bayes' Theorem.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (control in expositive or classroom practice classes)
Continuous assessment (two controls in laboratory practice classes)

assessment_rules: The evaluation consists of two parts: continuous assessment (30% of the final grade) and a final theoretical-practical written exam (70% of the final grade). Continuous assessment includes a control in expositive or classroom practice classes (10%) and two controls in laboratory practice classes (20%). In the extraordinary January resit and for students under differentiated evaluation, the final exam accounts for 80% and a laboratory test for the remaining 20%. Linguistic and spelling errors may be penalized in all assessments.
